Court filings show the Goldman Sachs Specialty Lending Group-led prepetition credit agreement carried about $122.5m of term loan principal, $6.5m of revolving loans and more than $190m of accumulated interest, fees and other obligations; an event-of-default notice was served in April 2026 and the company had been operating under expiring forbearance agreements after missing minimum EBITDA covenants in 2025. The franchisor (an Outback/Bloomin' Brands subsidiary) is providing a $5.5m DIP facility and a $26.3m stalking-horse bid for substantially all assets. Chrizza note: the upstream wire figure of '$449m debt' for this franchisee is not reconciled with these filings.

items.excerpt: On 2 November 2026 Karyopharm Therapeutics and an affiliate filed prepackaged Chapter 11 petitions in the Southern District of Texas (Case No. 26-90827) under a Restructuring Support Agreement backed by 100% of first-lien term lenders. Funded debt of roughly $276m (one source cites about $285m including other secured debt) - DIP roll-up, first-lien term loans and 1.5L/2L secured notes - receives 100% of reorganised equity, converting into about 55% of the company combined with stalking-horse bidder Ayrmid Ltd., plus contingent value rights. Existing lenders committed $55m of DIP financing; an alternative sale needs roughly $335.4m of net cash proceeds; existing common and preferred equity is cancelled. Closing is targeted for Q1 2027. Latham & Watkins advises the lender group.

items.title: Fitch U.S. Private Credit Default Rate at a record 6.3% TTM, ~88–90% from soft restructurings (PIK and deferrals ~50%, stressed extensions ~38%); U.S. leveraged loan default rate ~3.9% vs 4.5–5.0% forecast
items.query: Fitch U.S. private credit default rate record 6.3% published
items.excerpt: Fitch Ratings' U.S. Private Credit Default Rate reached a record 6.3% on a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026, flat from August. About 88-90% of default events were soft restructurings: interest deferrals and the introduction of PIK accounted for about 50% of events and stressed maturity extensions about 38%, with bankruptcies and liquidations a minor share. Industrials and Manufacturing and Consumer Products and Services had the highest sector default rates at 9.7% each. Fitch's broader U.S. leveraged loan default rate was about 3.9%, below its full-year 2026 forecast of 4.5%-5.0%.

items.title: Non-traded BDC tender queues persist into Q4 2026: 5% quarterly caps, sector requests 9–12%+, Blue Owl tech vehicle (OTIC) up to ~40%; flagship funds prorating
items.query: non-traded BDC tender offer redemption requests fourth quarter 2026 private credit
items.excerpt: Perpetual non-traded BDCs continue to cap repurchases at 5% of shares per quarter. Sector-wide tender requests have run at roughly 9% to over 12% at points in 2026, with Blue Owl's technology-focused vehicle (OTIC) seeing requests of up to about 40% in a single quarter; Blackstone Private Credit Fund, Blue Owl Credit Income Corp., Apollo Debt Solutions, HPS Corporate Lending Fund and Ares Strategic Income Fund have prorated tenders. Withdrawal requests exceeded $20bn globally in early 2026. Fitch notes new requests have begun to ease in the second half as rollover queues are processed, but net organic flows for unlisted BDCs have been negative in some quarters and trapped shares trade in a secondary market at discounts to NAV.

items.title: Restructuring infrastructure context: Weil Gotshal recommends firm-wide dissolution (28 Oct 2026); Serta remand damages of $261.13m plus 9% interest (7 Jul 2026); Atalian lender takeover converts ~66% of debt to equity (22 Sep 2026)
items.query: Weil Gotshal wind down restructuring practice announcement 2026 / lenders lawsuit uptier dropdown court ruling / Atalian lender takeover
items.excerpt: On 28 October 2026 Weil, Gotshal & Manges' management committee recommended an orderly wind-down and dissolution of the whole firm after partner departures and failed merger talks, with AlixPartners and Davis Polk advising; 9fin's Q3 league table had Weil joint-top with Kirkland & Ellis at 12 completed European restructuring engagements each, so active creditor and debtor mandates must move. On 7 July 2026 the Southern District of Texas bankruptcy court ordered participating lenders in Serta's 2020 uptier to pay $261.13m of contract damages plus 9% New York prejudgment interest (about $400m in total), holding that a cashless exchange counts as a payment under pro rata sharing. On 22 September 2026 Atalian completed a lender takeover converting about 66% of its debt into equity, extending the rest to 2031 and issuing EUR 100m of new super senior notes.
